args.sql:
SELECT
    t.transportregistry,
    (
        (t.totaldeliverytons / dh.hubcaptons) *
        t.deliverysuccessrate *
        (1 - t.vehiclebreakrate / 100)
    ) * 100 AS lpm,
    CASE
        WHEN (
            (t.totaldeliverytons / dh.hubcaptons) *
            t.deliverysuccessrate *
            (1 - t.vehiclebreakrate / 100)
        ) * 100 < 100 THEN 'Logistics Breakdown'
        ELSE 'Normal Operation'
    END AS status
FROM
    transportation AS t
JOIN
    distributionhubs AS dh ON t.transporthubref = dh.hubregistry;

parts.text:
Here is the SQL query that computes the Logistics Performance Metric (LPM) for all transportation operations:

```sql
SELECT
    t.transportregistry,
    (
        (t.totaldeliverytons / dh.hubcaptons) *
        t.deliverysuccessrate *
        (1 - t.vehiclebreakrate / 100)
    ) * 100 AS lpm,
    CASE
        WHEN (
            (t.totaldeliverytons / dh.hubcaptons) *
            t.deliverysuccessrate *
            (1 - t.vehiclebreakrate / 100)
        ) * 100 < 100 THEN 'Logistics Breakdown'
        ELSE 'Normal Operation'
    END AS status
FROM
    transportation AS t
JOIN
    distributionhubs AS dh ON t.transporthubref = dh.hubregistry;
```

The LPM is calculated using the formula:

> LPM = (totaldeliverytons / hubcaptons) * deliverysuccessrate * (1 - vehiclebreakrate / 100) * 100

The status is determined by checking if the LPM is less than 100, in which case it is labeled as 'Logistics Breakdown', otherwise it is labeled as 'Normal Operation'.
